subject: MSA & Order Form — output title, feedback license, and procurement path
messages:
From: Susan Keller <susan.keller@cloudvista.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: CloudVista Procurement <procurement@cloudvista.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form + MSA: Clarify output title and feedback license

Rafael —

Thanks for the draft Order Form and updated MSA. Legal reviewed and has two outstanding items we need to resolve before procurement can route for signature:

1) Output title: We expect our customers to retain title to outputs generated from our data (this is a core requirement for CloudVista products). The current redline assigns broader rights back to Redwood. Please confirm whether Redwood can carve a narrow exception for non-exclusive productization or whether customer retains exclusive title.

2) Feedback license: We saw the standard broad feedback license in the MSA. CloudVista cannot agree to any license that would permit training on our customer data or derived outputs. We can agree to a limited feedback license for bug fixes and anonymized model quality improvements, but only if those improvements are not used to retrain models that will be sold or rehosted in a way that could reproduce CloudVista outputs.

I attached a marked-up Order Form (CloudVista_OrderForm_MSARedline_v3.docx) with inline comments.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on (1) output title and (2) the scope and purpose limitation of the feedback license? If needed we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal and procurement through the language.

Best,
Susan Keller
Senior Counsel — CloudVista
---
Attachment: CloudVista_OrderForm_MSARedline_v3.docx (docx, 72KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Susan Keller <susan.keller@cloudvista.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA: Clarify output title and feedback license

Susan —

Thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Appreciate you flagging those two items. High-level positions from our side:

• Output title: Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers full, exclusive rights to use and commercialize outputs for their business purposes. We do not assert ownership of customer-specific outputs. The redline language you saw aimed to preserve rights for generic productization (e.g., improving system-level features or templates) but not to claim customer-title. I'm happy to accept a more explicit carveout: CloudVista retains title to outputs generated from your data; Redwood may retain a narrow, non-exclusive right to use de-identified aggregate signals to improve service quality across customers.

• Feedback license / training: We understand the sensitivity. Revised proposal: a limited, non-exclusive feedback license allowing Redwood to use feedback for debugging, metric analysis, and anonymized quality improvements, expressly excluding use for model retraining that would incorporate customer content or outputs in distributed models or third-party products. We can add a contractual prohibition and audit right for CloudVista to verify.

If that addresses your legal team's concerns, we can circulate specific redline language this afternoon. If you prefer, I'm available for a quick call at 2pm PT to align on exact text before you re-run procurement.

Couple of practical notes: Monica is our lead for legal redlines and governance; I'm looping her so we can turn around language quickly.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-08T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Order Form + MSA: Clarify output title and feedback license — proposed path

Team — FYI and quick alignment request. CloudVista legal pushed two asks (output title + feedback license). I proposed the positions below and asked to circulate redline language if we agree:

Proposed concessions (minimal):
- Accept explicit language that CloudVista retains title to outputs generated from their data (Order Form / MSA). Redwood to retain non-exclusive rights to use de-identified, aggregated signals for platform improvements only; no productization of CloudVista-specific outputs.
- Offer a narrowly scoped feedback license limited to debugging, anonymized metric improvements, and internal model quality research. Contracted prohibition on using customer data/outputs for retraining models that would be redistributed or hosted as new model artifacts; include an audit provision (redwood to provide attestation, CloudVista may request evidence once per year).

Risks / asks for legal ops:
- Laura: can we draft the exact MSA/Order Form language that captures the carrier-friendly carveout for de-identified signals while preserving our rights to improve the service? Try to avoid broad "training" definitions that are ambiguous.
- Monica: recommend the audit attestation wording and whether the once-per-year evidence request is acceptable. Also advise on whether we should offer a small operational concession (e.g., a two-week blackout period on certain logs) to reduce friction.
- Ben: if legal signs off, are we okay to accept these redlines within the current pricing band or do we need to escalate for commercial concession?

Attachment: internal-checklist-output-feedback.txt (internal stub) — I pasted the key bullet points below for reference. We need a turnaround today if possible; CloudVista is looking to route procurement tomorrow.

Action items:
1) Laura to produce redline language by 3pm PT.
2) Monica to confirm audit/attestation phrasing by 3:30pm PT.
3) Ben to confirm commercial OK (or threshold for escalation) by 4pm PT.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Susan Keller <susan.keller@cloudvista.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: CloudVista Procurement <procurement@cloudvista.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA: Clarify output title and feedback license

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the quick responses and for looping your legal/commercial colleagues. Procurement confirms the following acceptable path based on your proposals:

• Output title: CloudVista will retain title to outputs generated from our data. Redwood's permitted use of de-identified aggregate signals for platform improvements is acceptable with the explicit caveat that such signals cannot be reverse-engineered to reproduce CloudVista outputs.

• Feedback license: CloudVista accepts a limited, non-exclusive feedback license for debugging and anonymized quality improvements only. The MSA must expressly prohibit the use of CloudVista customer data or outputs in model retraining that would be redistributed or sold. We welcome an annual attestation and one-time evidence package (SOC2 summary) to confirm controls.

Procurement has the redline and will route for signature once we receive the updated Order Form and MSA language. Please send the redlines and the attestation text, and we'll start DocuSign.

DocuSign link (procurement): https://docusign.com/link/abc123
Attachments received: CloudVista_OrderForm_MSARedline_v3.docx, evidence-SOC2-summary.pdf

Best,
Susan Keller
Senior Counsel — CloudVista
CloudVista Procurement <procurement@cloudvista.com> — please schedule the DocuSign routing once Redwood sends the updated files.
